comment_box:
Douglas Collins, Secretary

U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

810 Vermont Avenue NW

Washington, DC 20420

RE: Reproductive Health Services, Docket Number 2025-14687

To Whom it May Concern:

I am submitting this comment opposing the proposed rule, “Reproductive Health Services.” This proposed rule would rescind veterans’ access to abortion care in cases of rape, incest, or life or health endangerment to the pregnant person. Maintaining narrow coverage of abortion care only when a physician certifies that the life of the patient is in danger will cause confusion among providers and jeopardize the lives and health of veterans.

I write as an individual committed to reproductive freedom and as a supporter of the American Association of University Women (AAUW), a nonpartisan nonprofit with over 140 years of advocacy for gender equity. AAUW is dedicated to ensuring affordable access to contraception and abortion care for all women regardless of location. I share AAUW’s belief that everyone has the right to make decisions about their own reproductive lives without government interference.

Abortion access is vital to women’s ability to control their lives, bodies, and futures. Yet this proposed rule would leave over 9 million veterans, including nearly 300,000 women veterans of reproductive age who rely on the Veterans Health Administration, without access to this essential medical care. The proposed rule will further exacerbate the disproportionate harm of abortion restrictions on Black women and women of color, who represent two in five female veterans.

To strip our nation’s veterans of a fundamental freedom is antithetical to the promise and responsibility of the Department of Veterans Affairs. I urge the Department to withdraw the proposed rule that would rescind access to abortion care for veterans and their loved ones.

Thank you for considering this comment.

Sincerely, Diane Johnson
